items.headline: Schedule your most used Copilot prompts
items.summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot now supports scheduled prompts that run automatically on daily, weekly, or monthly cadences, surfacing results when needed without manual intervention. Users can schedule recurring queries like team status updates, project summaries, or compliance checks to save hours of repetitive work. This feature is described as one of the most practical yet underused Copilot capabilities in 2026.
items.levelshiftAngle: LevelShift implements Microsoft 365 Copilot for enterprise clients and our own internal operations. Scheduled prompts directly address workflow automation gaps we see in Financial Services compliance reporting and Manufacturing quality monitoring engagements. Share this with the Microsoft practice team and add scheduled prompt examples to our Copilot adoption workshops.

items.headline: Agentforce Builder launches with conversational workspace and one-click agent simulations
items.summary: Salesforce Summer 26 release introduces Agentforce Builder, enabling teams to craft, test, and refine AI agents in a single conversational workspace with instant editing and one-click simulations with real-time debugging. items.headline: Air Canada ruled liable for AI chatbot false discount promise in landmark tribunal decision
items.summary: Air Canada was held liable by a tribunal after its AI chatbot falsely told a customer they could buy a regular ticket and apply for a discount after completing a trip. The airline denied the refund because the policy did not exist, but the tribunal ruled the company is responsible for information provided by its AI chatbot. This marks a significant legal precedent for enterprise AI liability.
items.levelshiftAngle: This validates LevelShift's Controlled Execution methodology and human-in-the-loop services. Our SOC 2 certification and governance playbooks prevent exactly this failure mode. Use this as a battle card when pitching Agentforce and chatbot implementations, emphasizing that LevelShift builds with testing, validation, and accountability frameworks. Relevant to our Salesforce Service Cloud and customer service automation engagements.

items.headline: EU AI Act high-risk system obligations take effect August 2 2026 with Article 50 transparency rules unchanged
items.summary: EU AI Act amendments approved June 16 2026 pushed standalone high-risk AI system compliance from August 2 2026 to December 2 2027. However, general-purpose AI enforcement and Article 50 transparency obligations remain in effect August 2 2026 with no extensions. Synthetic content labeling requirements for systems deployed before August 2 2026 are postponed to December 2 2026. Conformity assessments, technical documentation, CE marking, and EU database registration must be completed by August 2.
items.levelshiftAngle: LevelShift serves clients in scope of EU AI Act extraterritoriality via UK and Dubai offices, particularly in Financial Services and Healthcare where compliance is tightest. Our SOC 2 certification and AI governance playbooks are the proof points EU and UK clients will ask for before the August 2 deadline. Sales and delivery teams should confirm which active clients deploy general-purpose AI or synthetic content systems that fall under the unchanged Article 50 transparency rules and offer governance assessment workshops immediately.
